tracks.narration: A flip-flop remembers one bit — but only on command. What makes it latch?
Here's a D flip-flop — data in, clock in, and Q out. The triangle on the clock input means it's edge triggered.
Set up a clock signal toggling steadily, and a data signal moving in its own rhythm.
On every rising edge of the clock, Q samples whatever D is right then. Between edges, D can dance around freely and Q ignores it.
Q catches D on the rising edge — that one bit of memory is the cell behind every register and counter.
